source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵי֙ מ֣וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ וַֽיִּשְׁאֲלוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּיהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר מִ֣י יַעֲלֶה־לָּ֧נוּ אֶל־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֛י בַּתְּחִלָּ֖ה לְהִלָּ֥חֶם בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after [the] death of Joshua, and asked [the] sons of Israel of Yahweh, saying, Who will go up for us against the Canaanite[s] at the first, to fight against him?

en.L: And it was after the death of Joshua, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Who will go up for us against the Canaanites first, to fight against them?"
en.B: After Joshua died, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Which of us should go up first to fight against the Canaanites?"
en.R: After Joshua died, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for guidance. "Which tribe should go first to attack the Canaanites?" they asked.

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya kifo cha Yoshua, wana wa Israeli wakamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakisema, "Ni nani atakayetupandia kwanza dhidi ya Wakanaani, ili kupigana nao?"
sw.B: Baada ya Yoshua kufa, Waisraeli walimwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Ni nani kati yetu atakayepanda kwanza kupigana na Wakanaani?"
sw.R: Yoshua alipokwisha kufa, Waisraeli walimwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awaongoze. Wakamwuliza, "Ni kabila gani litangulie kwenda kuwashambulia Wakanaani?"

decisions.choice: after the death of Joshua: the book begins where the book of Joshua ends
decisions.reason: Joshua's death and burial are told in Joshua 24:29-31. The book of Joshua opened with the same kind of words, "after the death of Moses" (Joshua 1:1), and Judges now opens the next stage in the same way: the tribes must go on without the leader who brought them into the land. Judges 2:6-10 steps back and tells Joshua's death again, to begin the account of the generations that followed. Some events in this chapter are also told in Joshua (the taking of Hebron and Debir, Joshua 15:13-19), so the chapter may gather the tribes' campaigns as a summary rather than keep strict order of time.

decisions.choice: asked of the LORD: sought God's answer, probably through the priest
decisions.reason: To "ask of the LORD" is to seek a decision from God. In Israel this was done through the priest, who carried the Urim and Thummim for this purpose (Numbers 27:21). The same question is asked in 20:18, at the other end of the book, where the tribes fight one of their own.

decisions.choice: the Canaanites: the peoples of the land as a whole
decisions.reason: "The Canaanite" is singular in the Hebrew, a name for the people of the land taken together, as in verses 3 and 4 where it stands beside other peoples. Here it means all who still held the land Israel was to take.

decisions.choice: who will go up for us first: which tribe is to lead the attack
decisions.reason: The question is not who should fight but who should begin, leading the rest. The answer in verse 2 names one tribe, Judah.

decisions.choice: for guidance; Which tribe
decisions.reason: Readable says what asking the LORD meant (m2) and makes plain that the question is about which tribe should lead, since the answer is a tribe (verse 2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יְהוּדָ֣ה יַעֲלֶ֑ה הִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh, Judah will go up; see, I have given the land into his hand.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Judah will go up. See, I have given the land into his hand."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Judah is to go up. I have handed the land over to them."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "The tribe of Judah will go. I have already handed the land over to them."

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Yuda atapanda. Tazama, nimeitia nchi mkononi mwake."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alijibu, "Yuda ndiye atakayepanda. Nimeitia nchi hii mikononi mwao."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alijibu, "Kabila la Yuda ndilo litakalokwenda. Tayari nimeitia nchi hiyo mikononi mwao."

decisions.choice: I have given: a promise spoken as already done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act. Before the battle is fought God speaks of the victory as settled, as he did to Joshua at Jericho (Joshua 6:2).

decisions.choice: given into his hand: placed under his power
decisions.reason: To give something "into the hand" of someone is to put it in their control. Judah is spoken of as one person, the tribe named after Jacob's son.

decisions.choice: handed the land over to them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" for the tribe, where the Hebrew says "his hand"; Literal keeps the singular.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָה֩ לְשִׁמְע֨וֹן אָחִ֜יו עֲלֵ֧ה אִתִּ֣י בְגוֹרָלִ֗י וְנִֽלָּחֲמָה֙ בַּֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וְהָלַכְתִּ֧י גַם־אֲנִ֛י אִתְּךָ֖ בְּגוֹרָלֶ֑ךָ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִתּ֖וֹ שִׁמְעֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Judah to Simeon his brother, Come up with me into my lot, and let us fight against the Canaanite[s], and will go also I with you into your lot. And went with him Simeon.

en.L: And Judah said to Simeon his brother, "Come up with me into my lot, and let us fight against the Canaanites; and I also will go with you into your lot." And Simeon went with him.
en.B: Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come up with me into the territory allotted to me, and let us fight the Canaanites together. Then I will go with you into your territory." So Simeon went with them.
en.R: The people of Judah said to the people of Simeon, their relatives, "Come with us into the land given to us, and help us fight the Canaanites. Then we will go with you into your land." So the men of Simeon went with Judah.

sw.L: Naye Yuda akamwambia Simeoni ndugu yake, "Panda pamoja nami katika kura yangu, tupigane na Wakanaani; nami pia nitakwenda pamoja nawe katika kura yako." Naye Simeoni akaenda pamoja naye.
sw.B: Yuda alimwambia Simeoni ndugu yake, "Panda pamoja nami katika eneo nililopewa kwa kura, tupigane na Wakanaani pamoja. Kisha mimi nitakwenda pamoja nawe katika eneo lako." Basi Simeoni akaenda pamoja nao.
sw.R: Watu wa Yuda waliwaambia watu wa Simeoni, ndugu zao, "Njooni pamoja nasi katika nchi tuliyopewa, mtusaidie kupigana na Wakanaani. Kisha sisi tutakwenda pamoja nanyi katika nchi yenu." Basi watu wa Simeoni wakaenda pamoja na Yuda.

decisions.choice: Judah and Simeon: brother tribes whose lands were joined
decisions.reason: Judah and Simeon were both sons of Jacob and Leah (Genesis 29:33-35), and the tribe of Simeon received its towns inside the land of Judah (Joshua 19:1, 9). The tribes speak as the brothers they are named after.

decisions.choice: lot: the territory given by lot
decisions.reason: The land was shared out by casting lots before the LORD (Joshua 14:2; 18:10), so a tribe's "lot" is the land it received that way.

decisions.choice: territory allotted to me (B); the land given to us; the people of Judah, of Simeon (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "lot" means once and then says "territory". Readable speaks of the tribes as peoples rather than as two brothers, so that a young reader does not picture two men. Balanced and Readable say "them" and "Judah" where the Hebrew says "him".

decisions.choice: "kura" (L) and "eneo nililopewa kwa kura" (B) for the allotted territory
decisions.reason: Swahili "kura" is the lot that was cast, and by extension the share it gave, as the terms note sets for these books. Literal keeps the bare word; Balanced says that the land was given by lot, as the English Balanced says "territory allotted to me".

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַל יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־הַכְּנַעֲנִ֥י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֖י בְּיָדָ֑ם וַיַּכּ֣וּם בְּבֶ֔זֶק עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up Judah, and gave Yahweh the Canaanite[s] and the Perizzite[s] into their hand, and they struck them at Bezek, ten thousand man.

en.L: And Judah went up, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they struck them at Bezek, 10,000 men.
en.B: When Judah went up, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} handed the Canaanites and the Perizzites over to them, and they defeated 10,000 men at Bezek.
en.R: So Judah attacked, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} let them defeat the Canaanites and the Perizzites. At the town of Bezek they defeated 10,000 of their men.

sw.L: Naye Yuda akapanda, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia Wakanaani na Waperizi mkononi mwao, nao wakawapiga huko Bezeki, watu elfu kumi.
sw.B: Yuda alipopanda, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatia Wakanaani na Waperizi mikononi mwao, nao wakawashinda watu elfu kumi huko Bezeki.
sw.R: Basi watu wa Yuda walishambulia, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawawezesha kuwashinda Wakanaani na Waperizi. Katika mji wa Bezeki waliwashinda watu wao elfu kumi.

decisions.choice: the Perizzites; Bezek: a people of the land and a town whose site is uncertain
decisions.reason: The Perizzites are named beside the Canaanites as people of the land from Abraham's time (Genesis 13:7; 34:30). Bezek is not known for certain. A Bezek in 1 Samuel 11:8 lay farther north, near the Jordan, and may or may not be the same place.

decisions.choice: ten thousand: the word for "thousand" may also name a unit of fighting men
decisions.reason: As noted at Numbers 1, the word for "thousand" can also be used of a military or clan unit, which would give a smaller number of men.

decisions.choice: the LORD gave them into their hand: the LORD gave Judah the victory
decisions.reason: The words fulfil the promise of verse 2. The battle is told as the LORD's gift before it is told as Judah's deed.

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" before Bezek so the reader knows it is a place.

source.text: וַֽ֠יִּמְצְאוּ אֶת־אֲדֹנִ֥י בֶ֨זֶק֙ בְּבֶ֔זֶק וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ בּ֑וֹ וַיַּכּ֕וּ אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י וְאֶת־הַפְּרִזִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And they found Adoni-Bezek at Bezek, and they fought against him, and they struck the Canaanite[s] and the Perizzite[s].

en.L: And they found Adoni-Bezek at Bezek, and they fought against him, and they struck the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
en.B: They came upon Adoni-Bezek at Bezek and fought against him, and they defeated the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
en.R: At Bezek they met the ruler, Adoni-Bezek. They fought against him and defeated the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

sw.L: Nao wakamkuta Adoni-Bezeki huko Bezeki, wakapigana naye, wakawapiga Wakanaani na Waperizi.
sw.B: Walimkuta Adoni-Bezeki huko Bezeki, wakapigana naye, wakawashinda Wakanaani na Waperizi.
sw.R: Huko Bezeki walikutana na mtawala wa mji, Adoni-Bezeki. Walipigana naye, wakawashinda Wakanaani na Waperizi.

decisions.choice: Adoni-Bezek: "lord of Bezek", the ruler of the town
decisions.reason: The name means "lord of Bezek" and may be a title rather than a personal name. It is formed like the name of Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem (Joshua 10:1). Verse 7 shows him as a king who had ruled over other kings.

decisions.choice: they found: they met him in battle
decisions.reason: "Found" here means came upon or met with an enemy, as in 1 Samuel 31:3. The verse goes back over the battle of verse 4 to bring in its king.

decisions.choice: the ruler
decisions.reason: Readable says who Adoni-Bezek was, as his name and verse 7 show.

source.text: וַיָּ֨נָס֙ אֲדֹ֣נִי בֶ֔זֶק וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אַחֲרָ֑יו וַיֹּאחֲז֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ וַֽיְקַצְּצ֔וּ אֶת־בְּהֹנ֥וֹת יָדָ֖יו וְרַגְלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And fled Adoni-Bezek, and they pursued after him, and they seized him, and they cut off [the] thumbs of his hands and his feet.

en.L: And Adoni-Bezek fled, and they pursued after him and seized him, and they cut off the thumbs of his hands and of his feet.
en.B: Adoni-Bezek ran away, but they chased him and caught him, and they cut off his thumbs and his big toes.
en.R: Adoni-Bezek ran away, but they chased him and caught him. Then they cut off his thumbs and his big toes.

sw.L: Naye Adoni-Bezeki akakimbia, nao wakamfuatia, wakamkamata, wakamkata vidole gumba vya mikono yake na vya miguu yake.
sw.B: Adoni-Bezeki alikimbia, lakini walimfuatia, wakamkamata, wakamkata vidole gumba vya mikono na vidole vikubwa vya miguu.
sw.R: Adoni-Bezeki alikimbia, lakini walimfuatia na kumkamata. Kisha wakamkata vidole gumba vya mikono yake na vidole vikubwa vya miguu yake.

decisions.choice: thumbs of his hands and his feet: his thumbs and his big toes
decisions.reason: One word serves for both the thumb and the big toe. It is the same word used when blood was put on the right thumb and the right big toe of the priests at their ordination (Exodus 29:20; Leviticus 8:23).

decisions.choice: cutting off thumbs and big toes: a maiming that ended a man's power to fight or rule
decisions.reason: Without thumbs a man cannot grip a sword or a bow, and without big toes he cannot stand firm or run in battle. It also shamed him. Verse 7 shows that Adoni-Bezek had done the same to others.

decisions.choice: his thumbs and his big toes
decisions.reason: English has two words where the Hebrew has one; Literal keeps the Hebrew form "thumbs of his hands and of his feet".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹֽנִי־בֶ֗זֶק שִׁבְעִ֣ים׀מְלָכִ֡ים בְּֽהֹנוֹת֩ יְדֵיהֶ֨ם וְרַגְלֵיהֶ֜ם מְקֻצָּצִ֗ים הָי֤וּ מְלַקְּטִים֙ תַּ֣חַת שֻׁלְחָנִ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי כֵּ֥ן שִׁלַּם־לִ֖י אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיְבִיאֻ֥הוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיָּ֥מָת שָֽׁם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said Adoni-Bezek, Seventy kings, [the] thumbs of their hands and their feet cut off, were gathering under my table; as I have done, so has repaid to me God. And they brought him [to] Jerusalem, and he died there.

en.L: And Adoni-Bezek said, "Seventy kings, with the thumbs of their hands and their feet cut off, used to gather [scraps] under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me." And they brought him [to] Jerusalem, and he died there.
en.B: Adoni-Bezek said, "Seventy kings, their thumbs and big toes cut off, used to pick up scraps under my table. God has paid me back for what I did." They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
en.R: Adoni-Bezek said, "I once had seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off. They had to pick up scraps of food under my table. Now God has done to me what I did to them." They took him to Jerusalem, and he died there.

sw.L: Naye Adoni-Bezeki akasema, "Wafalme sabini, waliokatwa vidole gumba vya mikono yao na vya miguu yao, walikuwa wakiokota [makombo] chini ya meza yangu. Kama nilivyotenda, ndivyo Mungu alivyonilipa." Nao wakamleta [mpaka] Yerusalemu, naye akafa huko.
sw.B: Adoni-Bezeki alisema, "Wafalme sabini, waliokatwa vidole gumba na vidole vikubwa vya miguu, walikuwa wakiokota makombo chini ya meza yangu. Mungu amenilipa kwa yale niliyotenda." Walimleta Yerusalemu, naye akafa huko.
sw.R: Adoni-Bezeki alisema, "Zamani nilikuwa na wafalme sabini niliowakata vidole gumba na vidole vikubwa vya miguu. Walilazimika kuokota makombo ya chakula chini ya meza yangu. Sasa Mungu amenitendea yale niliyowatendea wao." Walimpeleka Yerusalemu, naye akafa huko.

decisions.choice: as I have done, so God has repaid me: the punishment matches the crime
decisions.reason: Adoni-Bezek himself sees that what was done to him is what he did to others. It is the rule of a like penalty for a like wrong that Israel's law gives (Exodus 21:23-25; Leviticus 24:19-20).

decisions.choice: God: one God, though a Canaanite king is speaking
decisions.reason: The word for God can also mean "gods", but the verb "has repaid" is singular, so the king speaks of one God who has judged him.

decisions.choice: seventy kings ... gathering under my table: conquered rulers kept like dogs
decisions.reason: The kings of the land each ruled one town and the villages around it (Joshua 12:9-24). Seventy may be a round number for a great many. To pick up scraps under a table is what dogs did (Matthew 15:27); the maimed kings were kept alive to be humbled.

decisions.choice: they brought him to Jerusalem: most likely the men of Judah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say who brought him. The men of Judah are the subject of the verses before, and verse 8 tells of their attack on Jerusalem. It could also be his own people, taking him home to die.

decisions.choice: [scraps] (L); scraps (B); scraps of food (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to gather or pick up; what was gathered under a table can only be the scraps of food that fell from it.

source.text: וַיִּלָּחֲמ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יְהוּדָה֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיִּלְכְּד֣וּ אוֹתָ֔הּ וַיַּכּ֖וּהָ לְפִי־חָ֑רֶב וְאֶת־הָעִ֖יר שִׁלְּח֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And fought [the] sons of Judah against Jerusalem, and they captured it, and they struck it to [the] mouth of [the] sword, and the city they sent in the fire.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it, and they struck it with the edge of the sword, and they set the city on fire.
en.B: The men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They struck it down with the sword and set the city on fire.
en.R: The army of Judah attacked Jerusalem and captured it. They killed its people with their swords and burned the city.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Yuda wakapigana na Yerusalemu, wakautwaa, wakaupiga kwa makali ya upanga, na mji wakauteketeza kwa moto.
sw.B: Watu wa Yuda walipigana na Yerusalemu, wakauteka. Waliupiga kwa upanga, wakauteketeza mji kwa moto.
sw.R: Jeshi la Yuda lilishambulia Yerusalemu na kuuteka. Askari wake waliwaua watu wa mji kwa panga, wakauchoma mji moto.

decisions.choice: Judah captured Jerusalem: an attack that did not hold the city
decisions.reason: Verse 21 says the Jebusites went on living in Jerusalem, and Joshua 15:63 says Judah could not drive them out. The city was not held by Israel until David took the stronghold (2 Samuel 5:6-9). This verse most likely tells of a raid that took and burned the city, or part of it, without Judah settling there.

decisions.choice: struck it with the edge of the sword: killed its people in battle
decisions.reason: "The mouth of the sword" is the sword's cutting edge, the part that "eats". To strike a city with it is to kill its fighting men and people, as in Joshua 10:28-39.

decisions.choice: the men of Judah (B); the army of Judah (R)
decisions.reason: "Sons of Judah" means the members of the tribe; here it is those who fought, so Balanced says "men" and Readable "army". Literal keeps the tribe's name in the Hebrew form.

source.text: וְאַחַ֗ר יָֽרְדוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בַּֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י יוֹשֵׁ֣ב הָהָ֔ר וְהַנֶּ֖גֶב וְהַשְּׁפֵלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And after went down [the] sons of Judah to fight against the Canaanite[s] dwelling [in] the hill country and the Negev and the Shephelah.

en.L: And afterward the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites living [in] the hill country and the Negev and the Shephelah.
en.B: After that the men of Judah went down to fight the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Negev and the foothills.
en.R: After that, the army of Judah went down to fight the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the southern desert, and the low hills in the west.

sw.L: Na baadaye wana wa Yuda wakashuka kupigana na Wakanaani waliokaa [katika] nchi ya milima, na Negebu, na Shefela.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo watu wa Yuda walishuka kupigana na Wakanaani waliokaa katika nchi ya milima, katika Negebu na katika nchi ya vilima vya chini.
sw.R: Baada ya hayo jeshi la Yuda lilishuka kupigana na Wakanaani walioishi katika nchi ya milima, katika jangwa la kusini, na katika vilima vya chini upande wa magharibi.

decisions.choice: the hill country, the Negev, the Shephelah: the three regions of Judah's land
decisions.reason: The hill country is the central ridge; the Negev the dry land to the south; the Shephelah the low hills between the ridge and the coastal plain (Deuteronomy 1:7; Joshua 10:40). The verse names the whole of Judah's territory; verses 10-17 tell of the campaign in it.

decisions.choice: went down: from the heights of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The tribe "goes down" from the high ground around Jerusalem (verse 8) to the lands south and west of it.

decisions.choice: the southern desert, the low hills in the west
decisions.reason: Readable describes the regions instead of naming them, as in Joshua 10:40. For "the army of Judah" see verse 8.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶל־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הַיּוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּחֶבְר֔וֹן וְשֵׁם־חֶבְר֥וֹן לְפָנִ֖ים קִרְיַ֣ת אַרְבַּ֑ע וַיַּכּ֛וּ אֶת־שֵׁשַׁ֥י וְאֶת־אֲחִימַ֖ן וְאֶת־תַּלְמָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Judah against the Canaanite[s] dwelling in Hebron, and [the] name of Hebron formerly [was] Kiriath-arba; and they struck Sheshai and Ahiman and Talmai.

en.L: And Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron; and the name of Hebron formerly [was] Kiriath-arba; and they struck Sheshai and Ahiman and Talmai.
en.B: Judah marched against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron, which used to be called Kiriath-arba, and they defeated Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai.
en.R: Judah attacked the Canaanites who lived in Hebron. Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba. There they defeated Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai.

sw.L: Naye Yuda akaenda dhidi ya Wakanaani waliokaa Hebroni; na jina la Hebroni hapo kwanza [lilikuwa] Kiriath-arba; nao wakawapiga Sheshai, na Ahimani, na Talmai.
sw.B: Watu wa Yuda walikwenda kupigana na Wakanaani waliokaa Hebroni, mji ambao zamani uliitwa Kiriath-arba, wakawashinda Sheshai, Ahimani na Talmai.
sw.R: Watu wa Yuda waliwashambulia Wakanaani walioishi Hebroni. Zamani Hebroni uliitwa Kiriath-arba. Huko waliwashinda Sheshai, Ahimani na Talmai.

decisions.choice: Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai: the sons of Anak whom Caleb drove out
decisions.reason: Joshua 15:13-14 tells the same victory as Caleb's, and verse 20 here says it too: Caleb, of the tribe of Judah, drove out these three sons of Anak. The scouts had seen them at Hebron forty-five years before (Numbers 13:22). Here the deed is counted to Judah as a tribe. "Sons" may mean clans as well as men, as at Joshua 15:14.

decisions.choice: Kiriath-arba: "the town of Arba"
decisions.reason: As at Joshua 14:15 and 15:13, the old name means the town of Arba, the greatest man of the Anakim and father of Anak.

decisions.choice: "watu wa Yuda" (the people of Judah) where a tribe acts as a group, through these chapters
decisions.reason: Hebrew names a tribe as one person ("Judah went"), and Literal keeps that. Swahili Balanced and Readable say "watu wa Yuda", "watu wa Efraimu" when the tribe acts with plural verbs, so that the reader does not take the name for one man. Where only the two ancestors are pictured (Judah and his brother Simeon, verses 3 and 17), Balanced keeps the names.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֔ם אֶל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י דְּבִ֑יר וְשֵׁם־דְּבִ֥יר לְפָנִ֖ים קִרְיַת־סֵֽפֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went from there against [the] inhabitants of Debir; and [the] name of Debir formerly [was] Kiriath-sepher.

en.L: And he went from there against the inhabitants of Debir; and the name of Debir formerly [was] Kiriath-sepher.
en.B: From there they went against the people who lived in Debir. Debir used to be called Kiriath-sepher.
en.R: From there the army of Judah went to attack the people of Debir. Debir's old name was Kiriath-sepher.

sw.L: Naye akaenda kutoka huko dhidi ya wenyeji wa Debiri; na jina la Debiri hapo kwanza [lilikuwa] Kiriath-seferi.
sw.B: Kutoka huko walikwenda kupigana na watu waliokaa Debiri. Zamani Debiri uliitwa Kiriath-seferi.
sw.R: Kutoka huko jeshi la Yuda lilikwenda kuwashambulia watu wa Debiri. Jina la zamani la Debiri lilikuwa Kiriath-seferi.

decisions.choice: the story told also in Joshua 15:15-19
decisions.reason: Verses 11-15 repeat Joshua 15:15-19 almost word for word. Here the attack on Debir is part of Judah's campaign in the south (verses 9-10).

decisions.choice: Debir, once Kiriath-sepher: a town in the hills south-west of Hebron
decisions.reason: Kiriath-sepher means "town of the book" or "town of the scribe". Joshua had struck Debir before (Joshua 10:38-39), but it had to be taken again.

decisions.choice: they (B); the army of Judah (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he", meaning Judah as one person. Balanced says "they" and Readable names Judah's army.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר כָּלֵ֔ב אֲשֶׁר־יַכֶּ֥ה אֶת־קִרְיַת־סֵ֖פֶר וּלְכָדָ֑הּ וְנָתַ֥תִּי ל֛וֹ אֶת־עַכְסָ֥ה בִתִּ֖י לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Caleb, [The one] who strikes Kiriath-sepher and captures it, and I will give to him Achsah my daughter as a wife.

en.L: And Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give him Achsah my daughter as a wife."
en.B: Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Achsah as a wife to the man who attacks Kiriath-sepher and captures it."
en.R: Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Achsah to be the wife of the man who attacks Kiriath-sepher and captures it."

sw.L: Naye Kalebu akasema, "Yeye atakayeupiga Kiriath-seferi na kuutwaa, nitampa Aksa binti yangu kuwa mke."
sw.B: Kalebu alisema, "Nitampa binti yangu Aksa awe mke wa mtu atakayeushambulia Kiriath-seferi na kuuteka."
sw.R: Kalebu alisema, "Mtu atakayeushambulia mji wa Kiriath-seferi na kuuteka, nitampa binti yangu Aksa awe mke wake."

decisions.choice: I will give him my daughter as a wife: a bride as the reward for a deed of war
decisions.reason: A father arranged his daughter's marriage. Offering her to the man who won a hard battle honored the winner and bound him to the family, as Saul's offer for killing Goliath did (1 Samuel 17:25; 18:17).

decisions.choice: the same words as Joshua 15:16
decisions.reason: Caleb's offer is given in the same words in Joshua 15:16, and the wording here follows that verse.

source.text: וַֽיִּלְכְּדָהּ֙ עָתְנִיאֵ֣ל בֶּן־קְנַ֔ז אֲחִ֥י כָלֵ֖ב הַקָּטֹ֣ן מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וַיִּתֶּן־ל֛וֹ אֶת־עַכְסָ֥ה בִתּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And captured it Othniel son of Kenaz, brother of Caleb, the younger than him; and he gave to him Achsah his daughter as a wife.

en.L: And Othniel son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, younger than he, captured it; and he gave him Achsah his daughter as a wife.
en.B: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
en.R: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured the town. So Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah to be his wife.

sw.L: Naye Othnieli mwana wa Kenazi, ndugu ya Kalebu, mdogo kuliko yeye, akautwaa; naye akampa Aksa binti yake kuwa mke.
sw.B: Othnieli mwana wa Kenazi, ndugu mdogo wa Kalebu, aliuteka, basi Kalebu akampa binti yake Aksa awe mke wake.
sw.R: Othnieli mwana wa Kenazi, ndugu mdogo wa Kalebu, aliuteka mji huo. Basi Kalebu akampa binti yake Aksa awe mke wake.

decisions.choice: Caleb's younger brother: most likely Othniel, possibly his father Kenaz
decisions.reason: The words "the brother of Caleb, younger than he" could describe Othniel or Kenaz. They are most naturally read of Othniel, as in 3:9. "Brother" may also mean a close relative of the same clan (Joshua 15:17).

decisions.choice: Othniel: later the first of the judges
decisions.reason: Othniel will rescue Israel from the king of Aram-naharaim and lead it for forty years (3:9-11).

decisions.choice: Caleb gave
decisions.reason: As in Joshua 15:17, Balanced and Readable name Caleb as the one who gave, since "he" could be read as Othniel.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹאָ֗הּ וַתְּסִיתֵ֨הוּ֙ לִשְׁא֤וֹל מֵֽאֵת־אָבִ֨יהָ֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַתִּצְנַ֖ח מֵעַ֣ל הַחֲמ֑וֹר וַיֹּֽאמֶר־לָ֥הּ כָּלֵ֖ב מַה־לָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when she came, and she urged him to ask from her father the field; and she got down from on the donkey, and said to her Caleb, What to you?

en.L: And it happened, when she came, that she urged him to ask her father for a field. And she got down from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What [do] you [want]?"
en.B: When she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. As she got down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"
en.R: When Achsah came to be Othniel's wife, she urged him to ask her father for a field. Then she got down from her donkey, and Caleb asked her, "What can I do for you?"

sw.L: Ikawa alipokuja, akamhimiza amwombe baba yake shamba. Naye akashuka kutoka juu ya punda, naye Kalebu akamwambia, "[Unataka] nini?"
sw.B: Alipokuja kwa Othnieli, alimhimiza amwombe baba yake shamba. Aliposhuka kutoka juu ya punda wake, Kalebu alimwuliza, "Unataka nini?"
sw.R: Aksa alipokuja kuwa mke wa Othnieli, alimhimiza amwombe baba yake shamba. Kisha akashuka kutoka juu ya punda wake, naye Kalebu akamwuliza, "Nikusaidie nini?"

decisions.choice: when she came: when she came to her husband as a bride
decisions.reason: Her coming is her arrival at Othniel's home at the marriage, as at Joshua 15:18. Her request may belong to the gift a father gave with his daughter when she married.

decisions.choice: she urged him: Achsah urged Othniel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "she urged him", here and in Joshua 15:18. The ancient Greek translation reads "he urged her", so that Othniel prompts Achsah to ask. The Hebrew is followed, since in verse 15 Achsah makes the request herself. This note is from general knowledge of the Greek and should be checked by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: she got down: slipped down quickly from the donkey
decisions.reason: The verb is rare (Joshua 15:18; Judges 4:21). It seems to mean a quick downward movement; getting down before an older man showed respect before a request (Genesis 24:64; 1 Samuel 25:23). Some take it to mean that she clapped her hands or called out.

decisions.choice: what to you?: what do you want?
decisions.reason: The short question asks what a person wishes or needs, as in 1 Kings 1:16.

decisions.choice: to Othniel (B); Achsah came to be Othniel's wife (R)
decisions.reason: As in Joshua 15:18, Balanced and Readable name the people the pronouns point to, and Readable says what her coming was (m1). Readable gives Caleb's question as a father's kind offer of help.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר ל֜וֹ הָֽבָה־לִּ֣י בְרָכָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֶ֤רֶץ הַנֶּ֨גֶב֙ נְתַתָּ֔נִי וְנָתַתָּ֥ה לִ֖י גֻּלֹּ֣ת מָ֑יִם וַיִּתֶּן־לָ֣הּ כָּלֵ֗ב אֵ֚ת גֻּלֹּ֣ת עִלִּ֔ית וְאֵ֖ת גֻּלֹּ֥ת תַּחְתִּֽית׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And she said to him, Give to me a blessing; for [the] land of the Negev you have given me, and you shall give to me springs of water. And gave to her Caleb upper springs and lower springs.

en.L: And she said to him, "Give me a blessing; since you have given me the land of the Negev, give me also springs of water." And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
en.B: She answered, "Give me a gift. You have given me land in the Negev; now give me springs of water too." Caleb then gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
en.R: She answered, "Please give me a gift. You have given me land in the dry south country, so give me some springs of water too." So Caleb gave her the upper and the lower springs.

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Nipe baraka; kwa kuwa umenipa nchi ya Negebu, nipe pia chemchemi za maji." Naye Kalebu akampa chemchemi za juu na chemchemi za chini.
sw.B: Alijibu, "Nipe zawadi. Umenipa ardhi katika Negebu; sasa nipe na chemchemi za maji pia." Basi Kalebu akampa chemchemi za juu na chemchemi za chini.
sw.R: Alijibu, "Tafadhali nipe zawadi. Umenipa ardhi katika nchi kavu ya kusini, kwa hiyo nipe pia chemchemi za maji." Basi Kalebu akampa chemchemi za juu na za chini.

decisions.choice: a blessing: a gift
decisions.reason: "Blessing" is used of a present given as a sign of goodwill (Genesis 33:11; 1 Samuel 25:27).

decisions.choice: the land of the Negev: dry land in the south
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry south of the land, where rain is scarce. A field there was of little use without water, so she asks for springs as well.

decisions.choice: springs of water; the upper and lower springs
decisions.reason: The word is used for bowls or basins, here pools or springs of water. "The upper and the lower springs" may be the names of two groups of springs, one higher than the other (Joshua 15:19).

decisions.choice: give me also
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "and you shall give me", a polite way of asking. Literal follows the wording of Joshua 15:19, the same request.

decisions.choice: the dry south country
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Negev is (m2), as in Joshua 15:19.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י קֵינִי֩ חֹתֵ֨ן מֹשֶׁ֜ה עָל֨וּ מֵעִ֤יר הַתְּמָרִים֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה מִדְבַּ֣ר יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּנֶ֣גֶב עֲרָ֑ד וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אֶת־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of [the] Kenite, father-in-law of Moses, went up from [the] city of the palms with [the] sons of Judah [to the] wilderness of Judah which [is] in [the] Negev of Arad; and he went and dwelt with the people.

en.L: And the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up from the city of palm trees with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah [into the] wilderness of Judah, which [is] in the Negev of Arad; and he went and lived with the people.
en.B: The descendants of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up with the people of Judah from the city of palm trees into the wilderness of Judah, in the Negev near Arad. They went and settled among the people.
en.R: Moses' father-in-law was a Kenite. His descendants went up with the people of Judah from Jericho, the town of palm trees, into the desert of Judah. This was in the dry south near the town of Arad. They went and settled there among the people.

sw.L: Na wana wa yule Mkeni, baba mkwe wa Musa, wakapanda kutoka mji wa mitende pamoja na wana wa Yuda [mpaka] nyika ya Yuda, iliyo katika Negebu ya Aradi; naye akaenda akakaa pamoja na watu.
sw.B: Wazao wa yule Mkeni, baba mkwe wa Musa, walipanda pamoja na watu wa Yuda kutoka mji wa mitende mpaka nyika ya Yuda, katika Negebu karibu na Aradi. Wakaenda wakakaa kati ya watu hao.
sw.R: Baba mkwe wa Musa alikuwa Mkeni. Wazao wake walipanda pamoja na watu wa Yuda kutoka Yeriko, mji wa mitende, mpaka jangwa la Yuda. Mahali hapo palikuwa katika nchi kavu ya kusini, karibu na mji wa Aradi. Wakaenda wakakaa huko kati ya watu.

decisions.choice: the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law: a desert people joined to Israel by marriage
decisions.reason: The Kenites were a desert clan linked with Midian (Numbers 10:29-32; 24:21). Moses' father-in-law is called a Kenite again in 4:11, where he is named Hobab. His family came into the land with Israel, as Moses had promised them a share in its good (Numbers 10:32).

decisions.choice: the city of palm trees: Jericho
decisions.reason: Jericho is called "the city of palm trees" in Deuteronomy 34:3 and 2 Chronicles 28:15. The Kenites had camped near it and now move south with Judah.

decisions.choice: the Kenite ... the people: the Hebrew has no name for the father-in-law and says only "the people"
alternatives: the Kenite, Hobab, father-in-law of Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives no name for Moses' father-in-law here. Some copies of the ancient Greek translation add a name, and some read "Amalek" in place of "the people", so that the Kenites settle among the Amalekites, as 1 Samuel 15:6 later finds them. The Hebrew is followed. This note is from general knowledge of the Greek and should be checked by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: he went and lived: the Kenite clan as one
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular, speaking of the whole Kenite family as one person, as Judah is spoken of in verse 3.

decisions.choice: They went and settled
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "they" for the singular "he" (m4).

decisions.choice: Jericho, the town of palm trees; the dry south
decisions.reason: Readable names the city (m2) and says what the Negev is.

source.text: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ אֶת־שִׁמְע֣וֹן אָחִ֔יו וַיַּכּ֕וּ אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֣ב צְפַ֑ת וַיַּחֲרִ֣ימוּ אוֹתָ֔הּ וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שֵׁם־הָעִ֖יר חָרְמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Judah with Simeon his brother, and they struck the Canaanite[s] dwelling [in] Zephath, and they devoted it to destruction; and called [one] [the] name of the city Hormah.

en.L: And Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they struck the Canaanites who lived [in] Zephath, and they devoted it to destruction; and [one] called the name of the city Hormah.
en.B: Then Judah went with his brother Simeon, and they defeated the Canaanites who lived in Zephath. They devoted the city to destruction, so it was named Hormah.
en.R: Then the people of Judah went with the people of Simeon, and they defeated the Canaanites who lived in the town of Zephath. They destroyed it completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So the town was called Hormah, which means "Destruction."

sw.L: Naye Yuda akaenda pamoja na Simeoni ndugu yake, wakawapiga Wakanaani waliokaa [katika] Sefathi, wakauweka wakfu kwa maangamizi; na [mtu] akaliita jina la mji huo Horma.
sw.B: Kisha Yuda alikwenda pamoja na Simeoni ndugu yake, wakawashinda Wakanaani waliokaa Sefathi. Waliuweka mji huo wakfu kwa maangamizi, kwa hiyo ukaitwa Horma.
sw.R: Kisha watu wa Yuda walikwenda pamoja na watu wa Simeoni, wakawashinda Wakanaani walioishi katika mji wa Sefathi. Waliuangamiza kabisa, kama mji uliotolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Kwa hiyo mji huo ukaitwa Horma, maana yake "Maangamizi."

decisions.choice: devoted it to destruction: gave the city wholly to God by destroying it
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of things or people given over to the LORD and taken out of human use, here by destroying them (Deuteronomy 7:2; Joshua 6:17-21).

decisions.choice: Hormah: a name made from the verb "devote to destruction"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like the verb and can be heard as "Destruction" or "Devoted place". Numbers 21:1-3 tells of Israel devoting the towns of this region and naming the place Hormah; here Zephath is taken and given the name. Hormah later counts among Simeon's towns (Joshua 19:4), so Judah keeps its promise to Simeon (verse 3).

decisions.choice: called: the naming is impersonal
decisions.reason: "He called" has no named subject and means "the city was called", as in Numbers 21:3.

decisions.choice: as given over to the LORD; which means "Destruction"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the term, as in Joshua, and gives the sense of the name so that the reader can hear how it links with the destruction.

decisions.choice: "kuweka wakfu kwa maangamizi" (L, B); "kuangamiza kabisa, kama mji uliotolewa kwa BWANA" (R), for the verb of devoting to destruction, through these chapters
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb means to give a city wholly to God by destroying it. Swahili "kuweka wakfu" is to dedicate, and "kwa maangamizi" says how, as the Pentateuch drafts do; Readable says plainly that the city was destroyed and why, as the English Readable does. The name Horma is then explained as "Maangamizi" (Destruction).

source.text: וַיִּלְכֹּ֤ד יְהוּדָה֙ אֶת־עַזָּ֣ה וְאֶת־גְּבוּלָ֔הּ וְאֶֽת־אַשְׁקְל֖וֹן וְאֶת־גְּבוּלָ֑הּ וְאֶת־עֶקְר֖וֹן וְאֶת־גְּבוּלָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And captured Judah Gaza and its territory, and Ashkelon and its territory, and Ekron and its territory.

en.L: And Judah captured Gaza and its territory, and Ashkelon and its territory, and Ekron and its territory.
en.B: Judah also captured Gaza, Ashkelon and Ekron, each with its surrounding territory.
en.R: Judah also captured the towns of Gaza, Ashkelon and Ekron, and the land around each of them.

sw.L: Naye Yuda akatwaa Gaza na mpaka wake, na Ashkeloni na mpaka wake, na Ekroni na mpaka wake.
sw.B: Yuda pia aliteka Gaza, Ashkeloni na Ekroni, kila mmoja pamoja na eneo lililouzunguka.
sw.R: Watu wa Yuda pia waliteka miji ya Gaza, Ashkeloni na Ekroni, pamoja na nchi iliyozunguka kila mji.

decisions.choice: Judah captured: the Hebrew text followed
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads that Judah "did not take" Gaza, Ashkelon and Ekron. That fits verse 19, where Judah cannot drive out the people of the plain, and the later chapters, where these cities are Philistine strongholds (3:3; 14:19; 16:1). The Hebrew says they were captured, which may mean they were taken for a time but not held. The Hebrew is followed. This note is from general knowledge of the Greek and should be checked by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron: cities of the southern coastal plain
decisions.reason: These are three of the five cities later held by the Philistines (Joshua 13:3). Joshua 15:45-47 lists them in Judah's land.

decisions.choice: each with its surrounding territory (B); the land around each of them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "its territory" once for the three cities; Literal keeps the repetition.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶתּ־יְהוּדָ֔הוַיֹּ֖רֶשׁ אֶת־הָהָ֑ר כִּ֣י לֹ֤א לְהוֹרִישׁ֙ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָעֵ֔מֶק כִּי־רֶ֥כֶב בַּרְזֶ֖ל לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And was Yahweh with Judah, and he took possession of the hill country; for not to dispossess [the] inhabitants of the valley, for chariotry of iron [was] to them.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Judah, and he took possession of the hill country; but [he could] not dispossess the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was with Judah, and they took the hill country for their own. But they could not drive out the people who lived on the plain, because those people had iron chariots.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was with the people of Judah, and they took over the hill country. But they could not drive out the people who lived on the plain, because those people had chariots made with iron.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja na Yuda, naye akaimiliki nchi ya milima; lakini [hakuweza] kuwafukuza wenyeji wa bondeni, kwa sababu walikuwa na magari ya chuma.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja na watu wa Yuda, nao wakaimiliki nchi ya milima. Lakini hawakuweza kuwafukuza watu waliokaa nchi tambarare, kwa sababu watu hao walikuwa na magari ya vita ya chuma.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja na watu wa Yuda, nao wakaitwaa nchi ya milima. Lakini hawakuweza kuwafukuza watu walioishi katika nchi tambarare, kwa sababu watu hao walikuwa na magari ya vita yaliyotengenezwa kwa chuma.

decisions.choice: not to dispossess: was not able to drive them out
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "not to dispossess", a short way of saying it could not be done (compare Joshua 17:12, "were not able to take possession").

decisions.choice: chariots of iron: war chariots fitted with iron
decisions.reason: As at Joshua 17:16, these were horse-drawn war chariots, probably made of wood with iron fittings. On flat ground they gave the Canaanites the advantage; in the hills they were of little use.

decisions.choice: the LORD was with Judah, yet they could not drive out the people of the plain
decisions.reason: The verse sets the two side by side without explaining them. In Joshua 17:18 Joshua had told Joseph's tribes that they would drive out the Canaanites "though they have iron chariots". The book goes on to give the LORD's own word on why the nations remained (2:1-3, 20-23).

decisions.choice: the valley: the low, flat land below the hills
decisions.reason: The word means a broad valley or plain. Here it is the lowland beside Judah's hills, most likely the coastal plain of verse 18.

decisions.choice: drive out; the plain
decisions.reason: For peoples, Literal says "dispossess" and Balanced and Readable "drive out", as in Joshua. Balanced and Readable say "plain" for the flat land meant (m4); Literal keeps "valley".

decisions.choice: "kuwafukuza" (drive out) for the verb of dispossessing a people, at every level, through these chapters; "kumiliki" (take possession) for taking land
decisions.reason: The one Hebrew verb means both to take possession of land and to drive out the people who held it. Swahili has no single word for both, so it says "kuimiliki nchi" of the land and "kuwafukuza" of the people, at every level, as the Deuteronomy drafts do.

source.text: וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ לְכָלֵב֙ אֶת־חֶבְר֔וֹן כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיּ֣וֹרֶשׁ מִשָּׁ֔ם אֶת־שְׁלֹשָׁ֖ה בְּנֵ֥י הָעֲנָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And they gave to Caleb Hebron just as had spoken Moses, and he dispossessed from there [the] three sons of the Anak.

en.L: And they gave Hebron to Caleb, just as Moses had said, and he dispossessed from there the three sons of Anak.
en.B: Hebron was given to Caleb, as Moses had promised, and he drove out the three sons of Anak from there.
en.R: As Moses had promised, Caleb was given the town of Hebron. Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak who lived there.

sw.L: Nao wakampa Kalebu Hebroni, kama Musa alivyosema; naye akawafukuza kutoka huko wana watatu wa Anaki.
sw.B: Kalebu alipewa Hebroni, kama Musa alivyoahidi, naye akawafukuza kutoka huko wana watatu wa Anaki.
sw.R: Kama Musa alivyokuwa ameahidi, Kalebu alipewa mji wa Hebroni. Kalebu aliwafukuza wana watatu wa Anaki walioishi huko.

decisions.choice: just as Moses had said: the promise to Caleb
decisions.reason: Moses had promised Caleb the land he walked on as a scout, because he followed the LORD fully (Numbers 14:24; Deuteronomy 1:36), and Joshua gave him Hebron on that word (Joshua 14:9-14).

decisions.choice: the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai
decisions.reason: These are the three named in verse 10 and Joshua 15:14. "Sons" may mean their clans as well.

decisions.choice: they gave: the giver is not named
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; Joshua 14:13 and 15:13 tell that Joshua gave Hebron to Caleb.

decisions.choice: was given; drove out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a passive so as not to name a giver the Hebrew does not name (m3), as in Joshua 15:13. For "drive out" see verse 19.

source.text: וְאֶת־הַיְבוּסִי֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֔ם לֹ֥א הוֹרִ֖ישׁוּ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב הַיְבוּסִ֜י אֶת־בְּנֵ֤י בִנְיָמִן֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the Jebusite[s] dwelling [in] Jerusalem not dispossessed [the] sons of Benjamin; and dwelt the Jebusite[s] with [the] sons of Benjamin in Jerusalem until the day the this.

en.L: But the Jebusites who lived [in] Jerusalem, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Benjamin did not dispossess [them]; and the Jebusites have lived with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
en.B: But the people of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem, and the Jebusites have lived there with the people of Benjamin to this day.
en.R: But the people of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem. The Jebusites still live there among the people of Benjamin today.

sw.L: Lakini Wayebusi waliokaa [katika] Yerusalemu, wana wa Benyamini hawakuwafukuza; nao Wayebusi wamekaa pamoja na wana wa Benyamini katika Yerusalemu mpaka siku hii.
sw.B: Lakini watu wa Benyamini hawakuwafukuza Wayebusi waliokaa Yerusalemu, na Wayebusi wamekaa huko pamoja na watu wa Benyamini mpaka leo.
sw.R: Lakini watu wa Benyamini hawakuwafukuza Wayebusi walioishi Yerusalemu. Wayebusi bado wanaishi huko kati ya watu wa Benyamini hata leo.

decisions.choice: Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites: the same as Joshua 15:63, told of Benjamin
decisions.reason: Joshua 15:63 says that Judah could not drive out the Jebusites of Jerusalem; here it is Benjamin that did not. Jerusalem lay on the border between the two tribes and was counted to Benjamin (Joshua 15:8; 18:16, 28), so neither held it. Judah had burned it (verse 8), but the Jebusites kept their stronghold until David (2 Samuel 5:6-9).

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time of writing
decisions.reason: The phrase speaks from the writer's own day, before David took the city.

decisions.choice: But the Jebusites ..., the children of Benjamin did not dispossess [them] (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the Jebusites first for emphasis. Literal keeps that order and supplies "them"; Balanced and Readable make one plain sentence. The opening "and" sets this against Judah's victories, so all levels say "But". For "drive out" see verse 19.

source.text: וַיַּעֲל֧וּ בֵית־יוֹסֵ֛ף גַּם־הֵ֖ם בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל וַֽיהוָ֖ה עִמָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up [the] house of Joseph, also they, [to] Bethel, and Yahweh [was] with them.

en.L: And the house of Joseph, they also went up [against] Bethel, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] with them.
en.B: The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with them.
en.R: The tribes that came from Joseph also went to attack the town of Bethel, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with them.

sw.L: Na nyumba ya Yusufu, wao nao wakapanda [kupigana na] Betheli, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [alikuwa] pamoja nao.
sw.B: Nyumba ya Yusufu nao walipanda kupigana na Betheli, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja nao.
sw.R: Makabila yaliyotokana na Yusufu nayo yalikwenda kuushambulia mji wa Betheli, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja nao.

decisions.choice: the house of Joseph: the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh
decisions.reason: Joseph's two sons became two tribes, which are often spoken of together as Joseph's house (Joshua 16:1-4; 17:14-17). Verses 22-29 turn from Judah in the south to these tribes in the center of the land.

decisions.choice: they also ... and the LORD was with them: as with Judah
decisions.reason: "They also" sets Joseph's campaign beside Judah's, and "the LORD was with them" repeats what verse 19 said of Judah.

decisions.choice: Bethel: an old holy place on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin
decisions.reason: Bethel, "house of God", was where God met Jacob (Genesis 28:19; 35:6-7). It lay on the boundary between Ephraim and Benjamin (Joshua 16:1-2; 18:13).

decisions.choice: [against] (L); against (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they "went up Bethel", with no word for "against". The context is an attack, so the word is supplied.

decisions.choice: the tribes that came from Joseph
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the house of Joseph" means (m1).

source.text: וַיָּתִ֥ירוּ בֵית־יוֹסֵ֖ף בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֑ל וְשֵׁם־הָעִ֥יר לְפָנִ֖ים לֽוּז׃

records.literal_gloss: And they caused to spy out, [the] house of Joseph, at Bethel; and [the] name of the city formerly [was] Luz.

en.L: And the house of Joseph sent spies to Bethel; and the name of the city formerly [was] Luz.
en.B: The house of Joseph sent men to spy out Bethel, which used to be called Luz.
en.R: They sent men to spy on Bethel. The town used to be called Luz.

sw.L: Nayo nyumba ya Yusufu ikatuma wapelelezi Betheli; na jina la mji huo hapo kwanza [lilikuwa] Luzu.
sw.B: Nyumba ya Yusufu ilituma watu kuupeleleza Betheli, mji ambao zamani uliitwa Luzu.
sw.R: Walituma watu kwenda kuupeleleza Betheli. Zamani mji huo uliitwa Luzu.

decisions.choice: they caused to spy out: they had the city scouted
decisions.reason: The form of the verb means to have others do the spying, so men were sent to look the city over.

decisions.choice: Luz: the old name of Bethel
decisions.reason: Genesis 28:19 tells that Jacob named the place Bethel, though the city was first called Luz. Verse 26 tells how the name Luz lived on elsewhere.

source.text: וַיִּרְאוּ֙ הַשֹּׁ֣מְרִ֔ים אִ֖ישׁ יוֹצֵ֣א מִן־הָעִ֑יר וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֗וֹ הַרְאֵ֤נוּ נָא֙ אֶת־מְב֣וֹא הָעִ֔יר וְעָשִׂ֥ינוּ עִמְּךָ֖ חָֽסֶד׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw the watchers a man coming out from the city, and they said to him, Show us, please, [the] entrance of the city, and we will do with you steadfast love.

en.L: And the watchers saw a man coming out of the city, and they said to him, "Please show us the way into the city, and we will deal with you in steadfast love."
en.B: The spies saw a man coming out of the city. "Please show us a way into the city," they said to him, "and we will show you faithful love."
en.R: The spies saw a man leaving the town. They said, "Please show us a way into the town. If you do, we will show you faithful love and spare your life."

sw.L: Nao walinzi wakamwona mtu akitoka mjini, wakamwambia, "Tafadhali, tuonyeshe njia ya kuingia mjini, nasi tutakutendea fadhili."
sw.B: Wapelelezi walimwona mtu akitoka mjini. Wakamwambia, "Tafadhali tuonyeshe njia ya kuingia mjini, nasi tutakutendea fadhili."
sw.R: Wapelelezi walimwona mtu akitoka mjini. Wakamwambia, "Tafadhali tuonyeshe njia ya kuingia mjini. Ukifanya hivyo, tutakutendea fadhili na kukuacha hai."

decisions.choice: the entrance of the city: a way into it
decisions.reason: The word means a way in. It may be the gate, or a hidden way such as a water channel, that would let them enter without a long siege.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal kindness that keeps faith
decisions.reason: As in Joshua 2:12-14, where Rahab helps the spies, chesed is the faithfulness owed to someone who has done you good. The spies promise to repay the man's help by keeping him safe, as verse 25 shows.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (L); faithful love (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:6, Deuteronomy and Joshua 2:12-14.

decisions.choice: If you do; and spare your life
decisions.reason: Readable says that the promise depends on his help and says what the kindness will be, as verse 25 tells.

decisions.choice: "fadhili" for the loyal kindness promised between people, at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note keeps "upendo usiokoma" for the faithful love of God and uses "fadhili" for the same word between people. Here the spies promise to keep faith with the man who helps them, so "tutakutendea fadhili" (we will deal kindly with you) is the natural Swahili.

source.text: וַיַּרְאֵם֙ אֶת־מְב֣וֹא הָעִ֔יר וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֶת־הָעִ֖יר לְפִי־חָ֑רֶב וְאֶת־הָאִ֥ישׁ וְאֶת־כָּל־מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֖וֹ שִׁלֵּֽחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he showed them [the] entrance of the city, and they struck the city to [the] mouth of [the] sword; and the man and all his clan they sent away.

en.L: And he showed them the way into the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword; but the man and all his clan they let go.
en.B: So he showed them the way in, and they struck the city down with the sword, but they let the man and his whole clan go free.
en.R: So he showed them the way in. They attacked the town and killed its people with their swords. But they let the man and his whole family go free.

sw.L: Naye akawaonyesha njia ya kuingia mjini, nao wakaupiga mji kwa makali ya upanga; lakini yule mtu na ukoo wake wote wakawaacha waende.
sw.B: Basi aliwaonyesha njia ya kuingia, nao wakaupiga mji kwa upanga, lakini wakamwacha yule mtu na ukoo wake wote waende zao salama.
sw.R: Basi aliwaonyesha njia ya kuingia. Walishambulia mji, wakawaua watu wake kwa panga. Lakini walimwacha yule mtu na jamaa yake yote waende zao salama.

decisions.choice: the man and all his clan they let go: spared like Rahab
decisions.reason: The story follows Joshua 2 and 6: an inside helper shows the way, the city falls, and the helper's family is spared (Joshua 6:22-25). Unlike Rahab, the man does not join Israel; he leaves the land (verse 26).

decisions.choice: struck with the edge of the sword
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: family
decisions.reason: Readable says "family" for the clan, as the terms for these books allow.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ הָאִ֔ישׁ אֶ֖רֶץ הַחִתִּ֑ים וַיִּ֣בֶן עִ֗יר וַיִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ ל֔וּז ה֣וּא שְׁמָ֔הּ עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went the man [to the] land of the Hittites, and he built a city, and he called its name Luz; that [is] its name until the day the this.

en.L: And the man went [to the] land of the Hittites, and he built a city and called its name Luz; that [is] its name to this day.
en.B: The man went off to the land of the Hittites, where he built a city and named it Luz. That is still its name today.
en.R: The man went to the land of the Hittites. There he built a town and named it Luz, and it is still called that today.

sw.L: Naye yule mtu akaenda [katika] nchi ya Wahiti, akajenga mji, akauita jina lake Luzu; ndilo jina lake mpaka siku hii.
sw.B: Yule mtu alikwenda katika nchi ya Wahiti, akajenga mji huko, akauita Luzu. Hilo ndilo jina lake hata leo.
sw.R: Yule mtu alikwenda katika nchi ya Wahiti. Huko alijenga mji, akauita Luzu, nao unaitwa hivyo mpaka leo.

decisions.choice: the land of the Hittites: the country to the north, beyond Israel's land
decisions.reason: "The land of the Hittites" names the lands north of Canaan, toward Syria (Joshua 1:4). The site of this second Luz is not known.

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time of writing
decisions.reason: As in verse 21. The old name the city had lost (verse 23) lived on in the town the man built.

source.text: וְלֹא־הוֹרִ֣ישׁ מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה אֶת־בֵּית־שְׁאָ֣ן וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֶיהָ֮ וְאֶת־תַּעְנַ֣ךְ וְאֶת־בְּנֹתֶיהָ֒ וְאֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֨י ד֜וֹר וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֶ֗יהָ וְאֶת־יוֹשְׁבֵ֤י יִבְלְעָם֙ וְאֶת־בְּנֹתֶ֔יהָ וְאֶת־יוֹשְׁבֵ֥י מְגִדּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֶ֑יהָ וַיּ֨וֹאֶל֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י לָשֶׁ֖בֶת בָּאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And not dispossessed Manasseh Beth-shean and its daughters, and Taanach and its daughters, and [the] inhabitants of Dor and its daughters, and [the] inhabitants of Ibleam and its daughters, and [the] inhabitants of Megiddo and its daughters; and was determined the Canaanite[s] to dwell in the land the this.

en.L: But Manasseh did not dispossess Beth-shean and its villages, and Taanach and its villages, and the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, and the inhabitants of Ibleam and its villages, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages; and the Canaanites were determined to dwell in this land.
en.B: But Manasseh did not drive out the people of Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam or Megiddo, or of the villages around them, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
en.R: But the people of Manasseh did not drive out the people who lived in Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam and Megiddo, or in the villages around those towns. The Canaanites refused to leave that part of the land.

sw.L: Lakini Manase hakuwafukuza [watu wa] Beth-sheani na vijiji vyake, wala [wa] Taanaki na vijiji vyake, wala wenyeji wa Dori na vijiji vyake, wala wenyeji wa Ibleamu na vijiji vyake, wala wenyeji wa Megido na vijiji vyake; nao Wakanaani wakakusudia kukaa katika nchi hii.
sw.B: Lakini watu wa Manase hawakuwafukuza watu wa Beth-sheani, Taanaki, Dori, Ibleamu wala Megido, wala wa vijiji vilivyoizunguka miji hiyo, kwa sababu Wakanaani walikuwa wameazimia kukaa katika nchi ile.
sw.R: Lakini watu wa Manase hawakuwafukuza watu walioishi Beth-sheani, Taanaki, Dori, Ibleamu na Megido, wala katika vijiji vilivyoizunguka miji hiyo. Wakanaani walikataa kuondoka katika sehemu hiyo ya nchi.

decisions.choice: Manasseh did not dispossess: the same failure as Joshua 17:11-12
decisions.reason: Joshua 17:11-12 lists these towns as Manasseh's and says the tribe could not take possession of them. Verses 27-36 go through the tribes one by one, and each record of failure is worse than the one before: here the Canaanites stay; in verses 32-33 Israel lives among the Canaanites; in verse 34 the Amorites drive Dan back.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the villages that belonged to a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the smaller settlements around it that depended on it, as in Joshua 17:11.

decisions.choice: Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo: strong Canaanite towns along the northern valleys
decisions.reason: These towns guarded the Valley of Jezreel and the coastal plain, the main roads across the north of the land (Joshua 17:11, 16).

decisions.choice: were determined: set on staying, refused to leave
decisions.reason: As at Joshua 17:12, the verb means to resolve or be willing to do something. The Canaanites held on to their land.

decisions.choice: the villages around them, said once
decisions.reason: As at Joshua 17:11, Balanced and Readable say "villages" once for the whole list; Literal keeps the repetition, saying "villages" for "daughters" as Joshua 17:11 does. For peoples, Literal says "dispossess" and Balanced and Readable "drive out", as in verse 19 and Joshua 16:10.

decisions.choice: because
decisions.reason: As at Joshua 17:12, Balanced joins the clauses with "because", since the second gives the reason for the first.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּֽי־חָזַ֣ק יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י לָמַ֑ס וְהוֹרֵ֖ישׁ לֹ֥א הוֹרִישֽׁוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when grew strong Israel, and he put the Canaanite[s] to forced labor; and dispossessing not he dispossessed him.

en.L: And it came about, when Israel grew strong, that they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not fully dispossess them.
en.B: Later, when Israel had grown stronger, they made the Canaanites do forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.
en.R: In time Israel became stronger. Then they made the Canaanites work for them as forced laborers. But the Israelites never drove all of them out.

sw.L: Ikawa, Israeli alipopata nguvu, wakawaweka Wakanaani chini ya kazi za kulazimishwa, lakini hawakuwafukuza kabisa.
sw.B: Baadaye, Waisraeli walipopata nguvu zaidi, waliwatumikisha Wakanaani kwa kazi za kulazimishwa, lakini hawakuwafukuza kabisa.
sw.R: Baada ya muda Waisraeli walipata nguvu zaidi. Ndipo waliwalazimisha Wakanaani kuwafanyia kazi. Lakini Waisraeli hawakuwafukuza wote.

decisions.choice: the same words as Joshua 17:13
decisions.reason: The verse repeats Joshua 17:13, with "Israel" for "the sons of Israel". Here it closes Manasseh's record and stands over the whole list that follows.

decisions.choice: forced labor: work demanded of a subject people
decisions.reason: As at Joshua 17:13, the word means a body of forced workers, or the labor they owed.

decisions.choice: dispossessing he did not dispossess: they did not drive them out completely
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, and the negative goes with the whole: they did not carry the work through (Joshua 17:13).

decisions.choice: when Israel grew strong: they could have driven them out but did not
decisions.reason: As at Joshua 17:13, the failure was not only weakness. Once Israel was strong enough, it chose to profit from the Canaanites' labor. The LORD's judgment on this follows in 2:1-3.

decisions.choice: they; them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he" for Israel and "him" for the Canaanites, each people spoken of as one. All levels say "they" and "them", as at Joshua 17:13. For peoples, Literal says "dispossess" and Balanced and Readable "drive out", as in verse 19 and Joshua 16:10.

decisions.choice: "kazi za kulazimishwa" (L, B) and "kuwalazimisha kuwafanyia kazi" (R) for forced labor, through these chapters
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names work demanded of a conquered people. "Kazi za kulazimishwa" (compelled work) says that plainly; Readable turns it into a verb, "they made them work for them".

source.text: וְאֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ לֹ֣א הוֹרִ֔ישׁ אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י הַיּוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּגָ֑זֶר וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֛י בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ בְּגָֽזֶר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And Ephraim not dispossessed the Canaanite[s] dwelling in Gezer; and dwelt the Canaanite[s] in his midst in Gezer.

en.L: And Ephraim did not dispossess the Canaanites who lived in Gezer; and the Canaanites lived in their midst in Gezer.
en.B: Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites went on living among them there.
en.R: The people of Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in the town of Gezer. So the Canaanites kept on living there among them.

sw.L: Naye Efraimu hakuwafukuza Wakanaani waliokaa Gezeri; nao Wakanaani wakakaa kati yao huko Gezeri.
sw.B: Watu wa Efraimu hawakuwafukuza Wakanaani waliokaa Gezeri, kwa hiyo Wakanaani waliendelea kukaa kati yao huko.
sw.R: Watu wa Efraimu hawakuwafukuza Wakanaani walioishi katika mji wa Gezeri. Kwa hiyo Wakanaani waliendelea kuishi huko kati yao.

decisions.choice: Ephraim and Gezer: the same failure as Joshua 16:10
decisions.reason: Joshua 16:10 says the same of Gezer and adds that its Canaanites were made to do forced labor. Gezer stood where the hills meet the coastal plain, guarding a main road; it came into Israel's hands only under Solomon (1 Kings 9:16).

decisions.choice: in his midst: among the people of Ephraim
decisions.reason: "His" is Ephraim, the tribe spoken of as one.

decisions.choice: drive out (B, R); in their midst, among them
decisions.reason: For peoples, Literal says "dispossess" and Balanced and Readable "drive out", as in verse 19 and Joshua 16:10. All levels say "their" or "them" for the singular "his" (m2).

source.text: זְבוּלֻ֗ן לֹ֤א הוֹרִישׁ֙ אֶת־יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י קִטְר֔וֹן וְאֶת־יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י נַהֲלֹ֑ל וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ לָמַֽס׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Zebulun not dispossessed [the] inhabitants of Kitron and [the] inhabitants of Nahalol; and dwelt the Canaanite[s] in his midst, and they became forced labor.

en.L: Zebulun did not dispossess the inhabitants of Kitron and the inhabitants of Nahalol; and the Canaanites lived in their midst, and they became forced labor.
en.B: Zebulun did not drive out the people living in Kitron or in Nahalol, so the Canaanites lived among them, though they were made to do forced labor.
en.R: The people of Zebulun did not drive out those who lived in the towns of Kitron and Nahalol. The Canaanites lived among them, but they had to do forced labor for Zebulun.

sw.L: Zabuloni hakuwafukuza wenyeji wa Kitroni wala wenyeji wa Nahaloli; nao Wakanaani wakakaa kati yao, wakawa [watu wa] kazi za kulazimishwa.
sw.B: Watu wa Zabuloni hawakuwafukuza watu waliokaa Kitroni wala Nahaloli, kwa hiyo Wakanaani walikaa kati yao, ingawa walilazimishwa kufanya kazi.
sw.R: Watu wa Zabuloni hawakuwafukuza wale walioishi katika miji ya Kitroni na Nahaloli. Wakanaani waliishi kati yao, lakini walilazimika kuwafanyia watu wa Zabuloni kazi.

decisions.choice: Kitron and Nahalol: towns of Zebulun
decisions.reason: Nahalol is most likely the Nahalal of Joshua 19:15 and 21:35, listed among Zebulun's towns. Kitron may be the Kattath of Joshua 19:15. Neither site is known for certain.

decisions.choice: became forced labor: were made to serve as forced workers
decisions.reason: As in verse 28 and Joshua 16:10.

decisions.choice: drive out; among them; though / but
decisions.reason: For peoples, Literal says "dispossess" and Balanced and Readable "drive out", as in verse 19 and Joshua 16:10. The last clause is set against what goes before: the Canaanites stayed, but under forced labor.

source.text: אָשֵׁ֗ר לֹ֤א הוֹרִישׁ֙ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י עַכּ֔וֹ וְאֶת־יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י צִיד֑וֹן וְאֶת־אַחְלָ֤ב וְאֶת־אַכְזִיב֙ וְאֶת־חֶלְבָּ֔ה וְאֶת־אֲפִ֖יק וְאֶת־רְחֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Asher not dispossessed [the] inhabitants of Acco and [the] inhabitants of Sidon, and Ahlab and Achzib and Helbah and Aphik and Rehob.

en.L: Asher did not dispossess the inhabitants of Acco and the inhabitants of Sidon, and Ahlab and Achzib and Helbah and Aphik and Rehob.
en.B: Asher did not drive out the people living in Acco or Sidon, or in Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik or Rehob.
en.R: The people of Asher did not drive out those who lived in the towns of Acco and Sidon, or in Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik and Rehob.

sw.L: Asheri hakuwafukuza wenyeji wa Akko wala wenyeji wa Sidoni, wala Ahlabu, wala Akzibu, wala Helba, wala Afiki, wala Rehobu.
sw.B: Watu wa Asheri hawakuwafukuza watu waliokaa Akko wala Sidoni, wala Ahlabu, Akzibu, Helba, Afiki wala Rehobu.
sw.R: Watu wa Asheri hawakuwafukuza wale walioishi katika miji ya Akko na Sidoni, wala Ahlabu, Akzibu, Helba, Afiki na Rehobu.

decisions.choice: Acco, Sidon and the other towns: the coast and hills of the north-west
decisions.reason: Acco was a harbor town on the coast; Sidon a great Phoenician city to the north. Achzib, Aphik (the Aphek of Joshua 19:30) and Rehob are in Asher's town list (Joshua 19:28-30). Ahlab and Helbah are not certainly known and may be two forms of one name.

decisions.choice: Ahlab, Achzib ...: the list goes on without "the inhabitants of"
decisions.reason: After Acco and Sidon the Hebrew names the towns alone. The sense is the same: the people of those towns were not driven out.

decisions.choice: drive out; the people living in
decisions.reason: For peoples, Literal says "dispossess" and Balanced and Readable "drive out", as in verse 19 and Joshua 16:10. Balanced and Readable say "the people living in" once for the whole list.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ הָאָ֣שֵׁרִ֔י בְּקֶ֥רֶב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֖י לֹ֥א הוֹרִישֽׁוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt the Asherite[s] in [the] midst of the Canaanite[s], [the] inhabitants of the land; for not he dispossessed him.

en.L: And the Asherites lived in the midst of the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, for they did not dispossess them.
en.B: So the Asherites lived among the Canaanites who lived in the land, because they did not drive them out.
en.R: So the people of Asher lived among the Canaanites of that land, because they had not driven them out.

sw.L: Nao Waasheri wakakaa kati ya Wakanaani, wenyeji wa nchi, kwa kuwa hawakuwafukuza.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo Waasheri walikaa kati ya Wakanaani waliokaa katika nchi hiyo, kwa sababu hawakuwafukuza.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watu wa Asheri waliishi kati ya Wakanaani wa nchi ile, kwa sababu hawakuwa wamewafukuza.

decisions.choice: the Asherites lived in the midst of the Canaanites: Israel became the minority
decisions.reason: Of Ephraim and Zebulun it was said that the Canaanites lived among them (verses 29-30). Here it is turned round: Asher lived among the Canaanites. The list grows darker as it goes on.

decisions.choice: he did not dispossess him: each people spoken of as one
decisions.reason: As in verse 28, the singular "he" is Asher and "him" the Canaanites.

decisions.choice: they ... them; drive out
decisions.reason: All levels say "they" and "them" for the singular (m2). For peoples, Literal says "dispossess" and Balanced and Readable "drive out", as in verse 19 and Joshua 16:10.

source.text: נַפְתָּלִ֗י לֹֽא־הוֹרִ֞ישׁ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֤י בֵֽית־שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ וְאֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בֵית־עֲנָ֔ת וַיֵּ֕שֶׁב בְּקֶ֥רֶב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֤י בֵֽית־שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ וּבֵ֣ית עֲנָ֔ת הָי֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם לָמַֽס׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Naphtali not dispossessed [the] inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and [the] inhabitants of Beth-anath; and he dwelt in [the] midst of the Canaanite[s], [the] inhabitants of the land; and [the] inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became for them forced labor.

en.L: Naphtali did not dispossess the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and the inhabitants of Beth-anath; and he lived in the midst of the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land; and the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became forced labor for them.
en.B: Naphtali did not drive out the people living in Beth-shemesh or Beth-anath, but lived among the Canaanites who lived in the land. The people of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath were made to do forced labor for them.
en.R: The people of Naphtali did not drive out those who lived in the towns of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath. They lived among the Canaanites of that land. But the people of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath had to do forced labor for Naphtali.

sw.L: Naftali hakuwafukuza wenyeji wa Beth-shemeshi wala wenyeji wa Beth-anathi; naye akakaa kati ya Wakanaani, wenyeji wa nchi; nao wenyeji wa Beth-shemeshi na Beth-anathi wakawa kwao [watu wa] kazi za kulazimishwa.
sw.B: Watu wa Naftali hawakuwafukuza watu waliokaa Beth-shemeshi wala Beth-anathi, bali walikaa kati ya Wakanaani waliokaa katika nchi hiyo. Watu wa Beth-shemeshi na Beth-anathi walilazimishwa kuwafanyia kazi.
sw.R: Watu wa Naftali hawakuwafukuza wale walioishi katika miji ya Beth-shemeshi na Beth-anathi. Waliishi kati ya Wakanaani wa nchi ile. Lakini watu wa Beth-shemeshi na Beth-anathi walilazimika kuwafanyia watu wa Naftali kazi.

decisions.choice: Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath: towns named after Canaanite gods
decisions.reason: Beth-shemesh means "house of the sun" and Beth-anath "house of Anath", a Canaanite goddess. Both are in Naphtali's list (Joshua 19:38). This Beth-shemesh is not the town of the same name in Judah (Joshua 15:10).

decisions.choice: he lived in the midst of the Canaanites: as Asher did
decisions.reason: Naphtali, like Asher (verse 32), lived among the Canaanites rather than the other way round, though it later made the people of two towns serve it.

decisions.choice: drive out; lived (B); They lived (R)
decisions.reason: For peoples, Literal says "dispossess" and Balanced and Readable "drive out", as in verse 19 and Joshua 16:10. The Hebrew "he lived" is the tribe; Balanced and Readable say it as the people.

source.text: וַיִּלְחֲצ֧וּ הָאֱמֹרִ֛י אֶת־בְּנֵי־דָ֖ן הָהָ֑רָה כִּי־לֹ֥א נְתָנ֖וֹ לָרֶ֥דֶת לָעֵֽמֶק׃

records.literal_gloss: And pressed the Amorite[s] [the] sons of Dan to the hill country; for not he allowed him to go down to the valley.

en.L: And the Amorites pressed the {{gender:children|sons}} of Dan into the hill country, for they did not let them come down to the valley.
en.B: The Amorites forced the people of Dan back into the hill country and would not let them come down into the plain.
en.R: The Amorites pushed the people of Dan back into the hills. They would not let them come down to the plain.

sw.L: Nao Waamori wakawasonga wana wa Dani mpaka nchi ya milima, kwa kuwa hawakuwaacha washuke bondeni.
sw.B: Waamori waliwasukuma watu wa Dani warudi katika nchi ya milima, wala hawakuwaacha washuke katika nchi tambarare.
sw.R: Waamori waliwasukuma watu wa Dani warudi milimani. Hawakuwaacha washuke katika nchi tambarare.

decisions.choice: the Amorites pressed Dan: the list ends with Israel itself driven back
decisions.reason: In every other tribe's record Israel fails to drive out the Canaanites; here the Amorites drive out Israel. Dan's land lay in the low hills and plain west of Benjamin (Joshua 19:40-46). Joshua 19:47 and Judges 18 tell how Dan later left to take land in the far north.

decisions.choice: the Amorites: a name for the peoples of the hill country and beyond
decisions.reason: "Amorite" is used, like "Canaanite", for the older peoples of the land, often those of the hills (Numbers 13:29; Joshua 10:5-6).

decisions.choice: the valley: the low, flat land below the hills
decisions.reason: As in verse 19, the word means a broad valley or plain, here the lowland where Dan's land lay.

decisions.choice: the people of Dan; the plain
decisions.reason: For "the sons of Dan" Balanced and Readable say "the people of Dan", as for Benjamin in verse 21. For "plain" see verse 19.

source.text: וַיּ֤וֹאֶל הָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת בְּהַר־חֶ֔רֶס בְּאַיָּל֖וֹן וּבְשַֽׁעַלְבִ֑ים וַתִּכְבַּד֙ יַ֣ד בֵּית־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיִּהְי֖וּ לָמַֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And was determined the Amorite[s] to dwell in Har-heres, in Aijalon and in Shaalbim; and was heavy [the] hand of [the] house of Joseph, and they became forced labor.

en.L: And the Amorites were determined to dwell in Mount Heres, in Aijalon and in Shaalbim; and the hand of the house of Joseph was heavy, and they became forced labor.
en.B: The Amorites were determined to stay in Mount Heres, Aijalon and Shaalbim, but the house of Joseph pressed hard on them, and they were made to do forced labor.
en.R: The Amorites refused to leave Mount Heres, Aijalon and Shaalbim. But the tribes that came from Joseph became stronger than they were and made them do forced labor.

sw.L: Nao Waamori wakakusudia kukaa katika Mlima Heresi, katika Ayaloni na katika Shaalbimu; lakini mkono wa nyumba ya Yusufu ukawa mzito, nao wakawa [watu wa] kazi za kulazimishwa.
sw.B: Waamori walikuwa wameazimia kukaa katika Mlima Heresi, Ayaloni na Shaalbimu, lakini nyumba ya Yusufu iliwalemea sana, nao wakalazimishwa kufanya kazi.
sw.R: Waamori walikataa kuondoka Mlima Heresi, Ayaloni na Shaalbimu. Lakini makabila yaliyotokana na Yusufu yakawa na nguvu kuliko wao, yakawalazimisha kuwafanyia kazi.

decisions.choice: Mount Heres, Aijalon, Shaalbim: towns on Dan's land, near the edge of the hills
decisions.reason: Aijalon and Shaalbim (Shaalabbin) are among Dan's towns (Joshua 19:41-42). Mount Heres, "mountain of the sun", may be the same as Ir-shemesh, "town of the sun", in Dan's list (Joshua 19:41), also called Beth-shemesh.

decisions.choice: the hand of the house of Joseph was heavy: their power pressed on the Amorites
decisions.reason: A heavy hand is power that weighs on others (1 Samuel 5:6). Where Dan could not hold its land, the tribes of Joseph, its neighbors, brought the Amorites under their control.

decisions.choice: were determined
decisions.reason: As in verse 27.

decisions.choice: pressed hard on them (B); became stronger than they were (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture of the heavy hand means (m2); Literal keeps it. Readable says "the tribes that came from Joseph", as in verse 22.

source.text: וּגְבוּל֙ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י מִֽמַּעֲלֵ֖ה עַקְרַבִּ֑ים מֵהַסֶּ֖לַע וָמָֽעְלָה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And [the] border of the Amorite[s] [was] from [the] ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela, and upward.

en.L: And the border of the Amorites [was] from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela, and upward.
en.B: The border of the Amorites ran from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and on up.
en.R: The land of the Amorites reached from the Akrabbim Pass and from Sela on up into the hills.

sw.L: Na mpaka wa Waamori [ulikuwa] kutoka mwinuko wa Akrabimu, kutoka Sela, na juu.
sw.B: Mpaka wa Waamori ulianzia kwenye Mwinuko wa Akrabimu, kutoka Sela na kwenda juu.
sw.R: Nchi ya Waamori ilienea kutoka Kipito cha Akrabimu na kutoka Sela, kwenda juu milimani.

decisions.choice: the ascent of Akrabbim: the Scorpion Pass, on the southern edge of the land
decisions.reason: Akrabbim means "scorpions". The pass climbs from the Arabah south-west of the Dead Sea and marks the southern border of the land (Numbers 34:4; Joshua 15:3).

decisions.choice: Sela: a place name, or "the rock"
decisions.reason: The word means "rock" or "cliff". It may name a place near the pass, or describe a well-known rock. It is probably not the Sela of Edom (2 Kings 14:7).

decisions.choice: the Amorites: the Hebrew text followed
decisions.reason: Some copies of the ancient Greek translation read "the Edomites", which would fit a border in the far south, near Edom. The Hebrew "Amorites" may use the name for the peoples of the hills as a whole (verse 34). The Hebrew is followed. This note is from general knowledge of the Greek and should be checked by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: the land of the Amorites reached; on up into the hills
decisions.reason: Readable says what the border marks and where "upward" leads, as in Joshua 15:3, where Akrabbim is the land's southern edge.
